[2020 summer phd math-stat — problem 1]

Suppose $(Y_1, \dots, Y_n)$ are observed, where $Y_i = \max(0, X_i)$ and $(X_1, \dots, X_n)$ are i.i.d. $N(\mu^*, \sigma^{*2})$ with $(\mu^*, \sigma^*)$ unknown. Define $R_i = \mathbb{1}\{Y_i > 0\}$. Let $\Phi(\cdot)$ be the $N(0,1)$ CDF. For $\theta = (\beta, \sigma)$ with $\beta = \mu/\sigma$, let $P_\theta$ denote $N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, and $\theta^* = (\beta^*, \sigma^*)$.
(i) Define an estimator $\hat\theta_1 = (\hat\beta_1, \hat\sigma_1)$ as the solution of $\mathbb{E}_\theta(R_1) = \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n R_i$ and $\mathbb{E}_\theta(R_1 Y_1) = \frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n R_i Y_i$. Find closed-form expressions for $(\hat\beta_1, \hat\sigma_1)$ (you may use $\Phi$ and its inverse).
(ii) Show that $(\hat\beta_1, \hat\sigma_1)$ are consistent estimators of $(\beta^*, \sigma^*)$.
(iii) Show that $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_1 - \theta^*) \xrightarrow{D} N(0, \tau_1)$ for some variance $\tau_1$; find a closed-form expression for $\tau_1$.
(iv) Write down the log-likelihood $\ell(\theta)$, and compute $\mathbb{E}_\theta\{\frac1n \frac{\partial \ell(\theta)}{\partial \theta}\}$ and $n\operatorname{var}_\theta\{\frac1n \frac{\partial \ell(\theta)}{\partial \theta}\}$ in closed form.
(v) The MLE $\hat\theta_2 = (\hat\beta_2, \hat\sigma_2)$ satisfies $\sqrt{n}(\hat\theta_2 - \theta^*) \xrightarrow{D} N(0, \tau_2)$ (you need not prove this). Find a closed-form expression for $\tau_2$.
(vi) Show that $\tau_1 \ge \tau_2$. Give a direct proof, instead of invoking the asymptotic efficiency of maximum likelihood estimation.

Let \(\phi=\Phi'\) denote the standard normal density. Write
\[
Z=\frac{X-\mu}{\sigma}\sim N(0,1),\qquad X=\sigma(\beta+Z),
\]
so that
\[
R=\mathbf 1\{Y>0\}=\mathbf 1\{X>0\}=\mathbf 1\{Z>-\beta\}.
\]
For shorthand, for a given \(b\in\mathbb R\), define
\[
p=\Phi(b),\qquad q=\Phi(-b)=1-p,\qquad c=\phi(b),
\]
\[
a=b\Phi(b)+\phi(b)=bp+c,
\]
and
\[
d=(b^2+1)\Phi(b)+b\phi(b)=(b^2+1)p+bc.
\]

---

## (i) Closed form for \(\hat\theta_1=(\hat\beta_1,\hat\sigma_1)\)

We have
\[
\mathbb E_\theta(R)=P_\theta(X>0)=P(Z>-\beta)=\Phi(\beta).
\]
Also,
\[
\mathbb E_\theta(RY)
=\mathbb E_\theta\{X\mathbf 1(X>0)\}
=\sigma \mathbb E\{(\beta+Z)\mathbf 1(Z>-\beta)\}.
\]
Using
\[
\mathbb E\{Z\mathbf 1(Z>-\beta)\}=\phi(\beta),
\]
we get
\[
\mathbb E_\theta(RY)=\sigma\{\beta\Phi(\beta)+\phi(\beta)\}.
\]

Let
\[
\bar R_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n R_i,\qquad 
\bar Y_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n R_iY_i=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n Y_i.
\]
The moment equations are
\[
\Phi(\beta)=\bar R_n,
\]
\[
\sigma\{\beta\Phi(\beta)+\phi(\beta)\}=\bar Y_n.
\]
Thus, on the event \(0<\bar R_n<1\),
\[
\boxed{\hat\beta_1=\Phi^{-1}(\bar R_n)}
\]
and
\[
\boxed{\hat\sigma_1
=
\frac{\bar Y_n}
{\hat\beta_1\bar R_n+\phi(\hat\beta_1)}
=
\frac{\bar Y_n}
{\hat\beta_1\Phi(\hat\beta_1)+\phi(\hat\beta_1)}.}
\]

If \(\bar R_n=0\) or \(1\), no finite solution exists. Since \(0<\Phi(\beta^*)<1\), those events have probability tending to \(0\), so any arbitrary convention there is asymptotically irrelevant.

---

## (ii) Consistency of \((\hat\beta_1,\hat\sigma_1)\)

Let
\[
p^*=\Phi(\beta^*),\qquad a^*=\beta^*p^*+\phi(\beta^*).
\]
By the strong law of large numbers,
\[
\bar R_n\to \mathbb E_{\theta^*}(R)=p^*
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]
and
\[
\bar Y_n\to \mathbb E_{\theta^*}(RY)=\sigma^*a^*
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]
Since \(0<p^*<1\), \(\Phi^{-1}\) is continuous at \(p^*\). Hence
\[
\hat\beta_1=\Phi^{-1}(\bar R_n)\to \Phi^{-1}(p^*)=\beta^*
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]
Also \(a(b)=b\Phi(b)+\phi(b)>0\) for all finite \(b\), and \(a\) is continuous. Therefore
\[
\hat\sigma_1
=
\frac{\bar Y_n}{a(\hat\beta_1)}
\to
\frac{\sigma^*a^*}{a(\beta^*)}
=\sigma^*
\quad\text{a.s.}
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\hat\theta_1\to \theta^*\quad\text{a.s., hence in probability}.}
\]

---

## (iii) Asymptotic distribution of \(\hat\theta_1\)

Let
\[
T_i=
\begin{pmatrix}
R_i\\
R_iY_i
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
R_i\\
Y_i
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Then
\[
m(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta(T_i)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\Phi(\beta)\\
\sigma\{\beta\Phi(\beta)+\phi(\beta)\}
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
p\\
\sigma a
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The derivative matrix is
\[
M(\theta)
=
\frac{\partial m(\theta)}{\partial(\beta,\sigma)^\top}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
c & 0\\
\sigma p & a
\end{pmatrix},
\]
since \(a'(\beta)=\Phi(\beta)=p\). Its inverse is
\[
M(\theta)^{-1}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
1/c & 0\\[4pt]
-\sigma p/(ac) & 1/a
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

We need the covariance of \(T_i\). We have
\[
\operatorname{var}(R_i)=p(1-p)=pq,
\]
\[
\operatorname{cov}(R_i,Y_i)
=
\mathbb E(Y_i)-\mathbb E(R_i)\mathbb E(Y_i)
=
\sigma a(1-p)=\sigma aq.
\]
Also,
\[
\mathbb E(Y_i^2)
=
\sigma^2\mathbb E\{(\beta+Z)^2\mathbf 1(Z>-\beta)\}.
\]
Using
\[
\mathbb E\{Z^2\mathbf 1(Z>-\beta)\}=p-\beta c,
\]
we obtain
\[
\mathbb E(Y_i^2)
=
\sigma^2\{(\beta^2+1)p+\beta c\}
=
\sigma^2 d.
\]
Therefore
\[
V(\theta):=\operatorname{var}_\theta(T_i)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
pq & \sigma aq\\
\sigma aq & \sigma^2(d-a^2)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

By the multivariate central limit theorem,
\[
\sqrt n\{\bar T_n-m(\theta^*)\}\xrightarrow{D}N(0,V(\theta^*)).
\]
By the delta method,
\[
\sqrt n(\hat\theta_1-\theta^*)
\xrightarrow{D}
N(0,\tau_1),
\]
where
\[
\boxed{
\tau_1
=
M(\theta^*)^{-1}V(\theta^*)M(\theta^*)^{-T}.
}
\]

Explicitly, evaluating \(p,q,c,a,d\) at \(b=\beta^*\) and writing \(s=\sigma^*\),
\[
\boxed{
\tau_1
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\dfrac{pq}{c^2}
&
\dfrac{s q}{c}\left(1-\dfrac{p^2}{ac}\right)
\\[14pt]
\dfrac{s q}{c}\left(1-\dfrac{p^2}{ac}\right)
&
s^2\left\{
\dfrac{d-a^2}{a^2}
-\dfrac{2pq}{ac}
+\dfrac{p^3q}{a^2c^2}
\right\}
\end{pmatrix}.
}
\]

---

## (iv) Log-likelihood, expected score, and score variance

For one observation \(Y\), the induced distribution has an atom at \(0\) of mass
\[
P_\theta(Y=0)=P_\theta(X\le 0)=\Phi(-\beta)=q,
\]
and for \(y>0\) density
\[
f_\theta(y)=\frac1\sigma \phi\left(\frac y\sigma-\beta\right).
\]

Thus the log-likelihood is
\[
\boxed{
\ell(\theta)
=
\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[
(1-R_i)\log \Phi(-\beta)
+
R_i\left\{
-\log\sigma+\log\phi\left(\frac{Y_i}{\sigma}-\beta\right)
\right\}
\right].
}
\]
Equivalently, up to the additive constant \(-\frac12\log(2\pi)\sum_i R_i\),
\[
\ell(\theta)
=
\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[
(1-R_i)\log q
+
R_i\left\{
-\log\sigma-\frac12\left(\frac{Y_i}{\sigma}-\beta\right)^2
\right\}
\right].
\]

For one observation, the score vector \(S_\theta(Y)\) has components
\[
S_\beta
=
-(1-R)\frac{c}{q}
+
R\left(\frac{Y}{\sigma}-\beta\right),
\]
and
\[
S_\sigma
=
\frac{R}{\sigma}
\left[
\left(\frac{Y}{\sigma}-\beta\right)\frac{Y}{\sigma}
-1
\right].
\]

Under \(P_\theta\), write \(Y=\sigma(\beta+Z)R\) with \(R=\mathbf 1(Z>-\beta)\). Then
\[
S_\beta=-(1-R)\frac{c}{q}+RZ,
\]
and
\[
S_\sigma=\frac{R}{\sigma}\{Z^2+\beta Z-1\}.
\]

One checks directly that
\[
\mathbb E_\theta(S_\beta)=0,\qquad \mathbb E_\theta(S_\sigma)=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{
\mathbb E_\theta\left\{\frac1n\frac{\partial\ell(\theta)}{\partial\theta}\right\}=0.
}
\]

Because observations are i.i.d.,
\[
n\,\operatorname{var}_\theta\left\{\frac1n\frac{\partial\ell(\theta)}{\partial\theta}\right\}
=
\operatorname{var}_\theta(S_\theta(Y)).
\]
Using the truncated normal moments
\[
\int_{-\beta}^{\infty} z\phi(z)\,dz=c,
\]
\[
\int_{-\beta}^{\infty} z^2\phi(z)\,dz=p-\beta c,
\]
\[
\int_{-\beta}^{\infty} z^3\phi(z)\,dz=(\beta^2+2)c,
\]
\[
\int_{-\beta}^{\infty} z^4\phi(z)\,dz=3p-(\beta^3+3\beta)c,
\]
we obtain the Fisher information matrix
\[
I(\theta)
=
\operatorname{var}_\theta(S_\theta(Y))
=
\begin{pmatrix}
I_{\beta\beta} & I_{\beta\sigma}\\
I_{\beta\sigma} & I_{\sigma\sigma}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
with
\[
I_{\beta\beta}
=
p-\beta c+\frac{c^2}{q},
\]
\[
I_{\beta\sigma}
=
\frac{\beta p+c}{\sigma}
=
\frac{a}{\sigma},
\]
and
\[
I_{\sigma\sigma}
=
\frac{(\beta^2+2)p+\beta c}{\sigma^2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
n\,\operatorname{var}_\theta\left\{\frac1n\frac{\partial\ell(\theta)}{\partial\theta}\right\}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
p-\beta c+\dfrac{c^2}{q}
&
\dfrac{a}{\sigma}
\\[12pt]
\dfrac{a}{\sigma}
&
\dfrac{(\beta^2+2)p+\beta c}{\sigma^2}
\end{pmatrix}.
}
\]

---

## (v) Asymptotic variance of the MLE

For the MLE, the limiting covariance matrix is the inverse Fisher information matrix:
\[
\tau_2=I(\theta^*)^{-1}.
\]

Evaluate everything at \(b=\beta^*\) and \(s=\sigma^*\). Let
\[
p=\Phi(b),\qquad q=\Phi(-b),\qquad c=\phi(b),
\]
\[
A=p-bc+\frac{c^2}{q},
\]
\[
B=bp+c,
\]
and
\[
D=(b^2+2)p+bc.
\]
Then
\[
I(\theta^*)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
A & B/s\\
B/s & D/s^2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{
\tau_2
=
I(\theta^*)^{-1}
=
\frac{1}{AD-B^2}
\begin{pmatrix}
D & -Bs\\
-Bs & As^2
\end{pmatrix}.
}
\]

---

## (vi) Direct proof that \(\tau_1\ge \tau_2\)

We show that
\[
\tau_1-\tau_2
\]
is positive semidefinite.

Let
\[
T=
\begin{pmatrix}
R\\
Y
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
S=
\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}\log f_\theta(Y)
\]
be the one-observation statistic and score. Let
\[
m(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta(T),\qquad
V(\theta)=\operatorname{var}_\theta(T),
\]
\[
I(\theta)=\operatorname{var}_\theta(S),
\qquad
M(\theta)=\frac{\partial m(\theta)}{\partial\theta^\top}.
\]
From above,
\[
M(\theta)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
c & 0\\
\sigma p & a
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Also, directly from the score formulas,
\[
\operatorname{cov}_\theta(T,S)=M(\theta).
\]

Now consider the random vector
\[
(T-m(\theta))-M(\theta)I(\theta)^{-1}S.
\]
Its covariance matrix is positive semidefinite. Since \(\mathbb E_\theta S=0\), its covariance is
\[
V(\theta)-M(\theta)I(\theta)^{-1}M(\theta)^\top.
\]
Therefore
\[
V(\theta)-M(\theta)I(\theta)^{-1}M(\theta)^\top\succeq 0.
\]
Premultiplying and postmultiplying by \(M(\theta^*)^{-1}\) and \(M(\theta^*)^{-T}\), respectively, gives
\[
M^{-1}VM^{-T}-I^{-1}\succeq 0.
\]
But
\[
\tau_1=M^{-1}VM^{-T},
\qquad
\tau_2=I^{-1},
\]
all evaluated at \(\theta^*\). Hence
\[
\boxed{\tau_1-\tau_2\succeq 0,}
\]
i.e.
\[
\boxed{\tau_1\ge \tau_2}
\]
in the Loewner positive-semidefinite order.

\int_{-\beta}^{\infty} z^2\phi(z)\,dz=p-\beta c,
\]
\[
\int_{-\beta}^{\infty} z^3\phi(z)\,dz=(\beta^2+2)c,
\]
\[
\int_{-\beta}^{\infty} z^4\phi(z)\,dz=3p-(\beta^3+3\beta)c,
\]
we obtain the Fisher information matrix
\[
I(\theta)
=
\operatorname{var}_\theta(S_\theta(Y))
=
\begin{pmatrix}
I_{\beta\beta} & I_{\beta\sigma}\\
I_{\beta\sigma} & I_{\sigma\sigma}
\end{pmatrix},
\]
with
\[
I_{\beta\beta}
=
p-\beta c+\frac{c^2}{q},
\]
\[
I_{\beta\sigma}
=
\frac{\beta p+c}{\sigma}
=
\frac{a}{\sigma},
\]
and
\[
I_{\sigma\sigma}
=
\frac{(\beta^2+2)p+\beta c}{\sigma^2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{
n\,\operatorname{var}_\theta\left\{\frac1n\frac{\partial\ell(\theta)}{\partial\theta}\right\}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
p-\beta c+\dfrac{c^2}{q}
&
\dfrac{a}{\sigma}
\\[12pt]
\dfrac{a}{\sigma}
&
\dfrac{(\beta^2+2)p+\beta c}{\sigma^2}
\end{pmatrix}.
}
\]

---

## (v) Asymptotic variance of the MLE

For the MLE, the limiting covariance matrix is the inverse Fisher information matrix:
\[
\tau_2=I(\theta^*)^{-1}.
\]

Evaluate everything at \(b=\beta^*\) and \(s=\sigma^*\). Let
\[
p=\Phi(b),\qquad q=\Phi(-b),\qquad c=\phi(b),
\]
\[
A=p-bc+\frac{c^2}{q},
\]
\[
B=bp+c,
\]
and
\[
D=(b^2+2)p+bc.
\]
Then
\[
I(\theta^*)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
A & B/s\\
B/s & D/s^2
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{
\tau_2
=
I(\theta^*)^{-1}
=
\frac{1}{AD-B^2}
\begin{pmatrix}
D & -Bs\\
-Bs & As^2
\end{pmatrix}.
}
\]

---

## (vi) Direct proof that \(\tau_1\ge \tau_2\)

We show that
\[
\tau_1-\tau_2
\]
is positive semidefinite.

Let
\[
T=
\begin{pmatrix}
R\\
Y
\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
S=
\frac{\partial}{\partial\theta}\log f_\theta(Y)
\]
be the one-observation statistic and score. Let
\[
m(\theta)=\mathbb E_\theta(T),\qquad
V(\theta)=\operatorname{var}_\theta(T),
\]
\[
I(\theta)=\operatorname{var}_\theta(S),
\qquad
M(\theta)=\frac{\partial m(\theta)}{\partial\theta^\top}.
\]
From above,
\[
M(\theta)
=
\begin{pmatrix}
c & 0\\
\sigma p & a
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Also, directly from the score formulas,
\[
\operatorname{cov}_\theta(T,S)=M(\theta).
\]

Now consider the random vector
\[
(T-m(\theta))-M(\theta)I(\theta)^{-1}S.
\]
Its covariance matrix is positive semidefinite. Since \(\mathbb E_\theta S=0\), its covariance is
\[
V(\theta)-M(\theta)I(\theta)^{-1}M(\theta)^\top.
\]
Therefore
\[
V(\theta)-M(\theta)I(\theta)^{-1}M(\theta)^\top\succeq 0.
\]
Premultiplying and postmultiplying by \(M(\theta^*)^{-1}\) and \(M(\theta^*)^{-T}\), respectively, gives
\[
M^{-1}VM^{-T}-I^{-1}\succeq 0.
\]
But
\[
\tau_1=M^{-1}VM^{-T},
\qquad
\tau_2=I^{-1},
\]
all evaluated at \(\theta^*\). Hence
\[
\boxed{\tau_1-\tau_2\succeq 0,}
\]
i.e.
\[
\boxed{\tau_1\ge \tau_2}
\]
in the Loewner positive-semidefinite order.
